title: Fabrication of Pt-decorated MXene–chitosan nanocomposite electrodes for non-enzymatic electrochemical detection of biomolecules
content: Cholesterol and hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) are essential biomolecules for maintaining the physical equilibrium, and their abnormal levels cause cancer and several cardiovascular diseases. To address the drawbacks of enzymatic techniques, including poor stability, high fabrication cost, and sensitivity to environmental conditions, a platinum nanoparticle (Pt) anchored MXene–chitosan composite (Pt/MX–Chit) was coated on an ITO substrate to develop a robust non-enzymatic platform. The integration of highly conductive MXene, electrocatalytically active Pt nanoparticles, and a biocompatible, film-forming chitosan matrix enables efficient electron transfer, improves the structural stability, and increases the number of surface-active sites compared to the existing non-enzymatic platforms. The fabricated electrode provides enzyme-free cholesterol detection by the catalytic oxidation of cholesterol and H2O2 by catalytic reduction. The structural characteristics and surface morphology of the synthesized materials were examined by SEM, XRD, TEM, AFM, and FTIR. The developed sensor exhibited a linear response to H2O2 concentration (0–160 µM) with a sensitivity of 1.29 µA µM−1, and an estimated LOD value of 4.57 µM and LOQ of 15.25 µM, which shows the strong catalytic reduction capability of the Pt/MX-Chit composite electrode interface. Non-enzymatic cholesterol detection was also performed with a positive response within the range of 0–20 µM through the oxidation of cholesterol in the anodic oxidation region. The sensor achieved a sensitivity of 14.6 µA µM−1. The estimated LOD and LOQ are 0.30 µM and 1.01 µM, respectively. The fabricated Pt/MX-Chit-ITO electrode offers a cost-effective and fast detection platform for biosensing applications.
